mask_effectiveness.structurally_unmaskable_note: these (outcome, configuration) groups carry exactly one companion, because §8.1's spectrum and class arms pair with B alone, so their companion label is not hidden and could not be. Under the full and no-spectrum designs that costs nothing: the singleton outcomes are the spectrum rungs and the class companion, and no registered estimand reads them as an OUTCOME -- F8 reads D(B <- R_j+-) and F9 reads D(B <- CL), both with B as the outcome and masked among its many companions. Under §8.6's REDUCED design it costs something and the cost is stated rather than implied: B has exactly two companions (A and the class companion) and is masked among them, while A and CL each have only B, so D(A <- B) -- a registered reduced-design estimand -- and any CL-as-outcome quantity are analysed with their companion identity visible. The masked phase protects D(B <- A), D(B <- CL) and Lambda on that design, and does not protect the reciprocal direction. This sentence used to assert the full-design case unconditionally, which is false for a reduced replication
